examples.question_text:
Students were asked whether they study Music and play soccer.

$\begin{array}{l|cc|c}&\text{Music}&\text{Not Music}&\text{Total}\\\hline\text{Soccer}&8&12&20\\\text{Not Soccer}&7&13&20\\\hline\text{Total}&15&25&40\end{array}$

a. How many study Music and play soccer?
b. How many study Music? How many do not play soccer?
c. One student is chosen at random. Find the probabilities that they study Music and play soccer, and that they study Music.
examples.solution_text:
a. The Music column and Soccer row meet at $8$.

b. The Music column total is $15$. The Not Soccer row total is $20$.

c. The denominator is the grand total, $40$.
$\begin{aligned}P(\text{Music and soccer})&=\frac{8}{40}\\&=\frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}P(\text{Music})&=\frac{15}{40}\\&=\frac{3}{8}\end{aligned}$

The Choir row gives the first missing cell:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}19-8\\&=11\end{aligned}$
The grand total gives the Not Choir row total:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}46-19\\&=27\end{aligned}$
Complete that row:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}27-9\\&=18\end{aligned}$
Add down the Not Drama column:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}8+18\\&=26\end{aligned}$

$\begin{array}{l|cc|c}&\text{Drama}&\text{Not Drama}&\text{Total}\\\hline\text{Choir}&11&8&19\\\text{Not Choir}&9&18&27\\\hline\text{Total}&20&26&46\end{array}$

examples.question_text: Of $35$ students, $21$ study French ($F$), $16$ play basketball ($B$), and $9$ do both. Construct a Venn diagram showing all four regions.
Of $40$ students, $25$ study Geography ($G$), $22$ play hockey ($H$), and $5$ do neither. Find how many do both and construct the completed Venn diagram.
Of $42$ students, $24$ study German ($G$), $10$ study German and play tennis ($T$), and $6$ do neither. Construct a Venn diagram and find how many play tennis altogether.

Construct a two-way table for each survey.

a. Of $80$ students, $30$ study Photography. Of these, $11$ also study Coding. Among those who do not study Photography, $32$ do not study Coding.

b. Of $90$ students, two-thirds are girls. There are $18$ boys who study Italian. Twice as many girls as boys do not study Italian. Find how many girls study Italian.
examples.solution_text:
a. Photography but not Coding:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}30-11\\&=19\end{aligned}$
Not Photography:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}80-30\\&=50\end{aligned}$
Coding but not Photography:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}50-32\\&=18\end{aligned}$
Add across and down for the totals.

$\begin{array}{l|cc|c}&\text{Photography}&\text{Not Photography}&\text{Total}\\\hline\text{Coding}&11&18&29\\\text{Not Coding}&19&32&51\\\hline\text{Total}&30&50&80\end{array}$

b. Girls:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{2}{3}\times90\\&=60\end{aligned}$
Boys:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}90-60\\&=30\end{aligned}$
Boys who do not study Italian:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}30-18\\&=12\end{aligned}$
Girls who do not study Italian:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2\times12\\&=24\end{aligned}$
Girls who study Italian:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}60-24\\&=36\end{aligned}$

$\begin{array}{l|cc|c}&\text{Italian}&\text{Not Italian}&\text{Total}\\\hline\text{Girls}&36&24&60\\\text{Boys}&18&12&30\\\hline\text{Total}&54&36&90\end{array}$

The overlap gives Chinese and Soccer: $7$.
Chinese only gives Chinese and Not Soccer: $8$.
Soccer only gives Not Chinese and Soccer: $11$.
Neither gives Not Chinese and Not Soccer: $4$.
Add across and down for the totals.

$\begin{array}{l|cc|c}&\text{Chinese}&\text{Not Chinese}&\text{Total}\\\hline\text{Soccer}&7&11&18\\\text{Not Soccer}&8&4&12\\\hline\text{Total}&15&15&30\end{array}$
